name: table
title: Table
description: Invoices, transaction histories, and small collections of structured records.
docs:
## Installation ```install npx shadcn@latest add @cadence/table ``` ## Usage ```tsx import { Table, TableBody, TableCaption, TableCell, TableHead, TableHeader, TableRow, } from "@/components/cadence/table"; export function Invoices() { return ( Recent invoices. Invoice Amount INV-001 $250.00
); } ``` ## Footer totals `TableFooter` renders a native `tfoot`. Spans and numeric alignment are caller-owned. ```tsx Total $750.00 ``` ## Selected rows Selection state belongs to the application. A data attribute supplies the visual state; add a named checkbox when selection must be interactive. Setting this attribute alone does not make a row a control or announce selection. ```tsx INV-001 Paid ``` ## When to use - Invoice summaries with amounts and payment states. - Transaction histories with a few consistent columns. - Small record collections where column comparisons matter. ## When not to use - For page layout: use CSS grid or flex. - For large collections needing sorting, filtering, pagination, or virtualization: compose those behaviours in the application; Table only supplies markup and styles. - For independent summaries with no column relationships: use cards or a list. ## API All eight exports accept `React.ComponentProps` for their native element, including `children`, `className`, `style`, event handlers, ARIA attributes and React 19 `ref`. Classes merge last. No custom props or defaults are added. | Export | Element | | --- | --- | | `Table` | `table` | | `TableHeader` | `thead` | | `TableBody` | `tbody` | | `TableFooter` | `tfoot` | | `TableRow` | `tr` | | `TableHead` | `th` | | `TableCell` | `td` | | `TableCaption` | `caption` | Each part's slot is its kebab-case name: `table`, `table-header`, `table-body`, `table-footer`, `table-row`, `table-head`, `table-cell`, and `table-caption`. `Table` also creates a `div` with `data-slot="table-container"` and `relative w-full overflow-x-auto`. Its props, classes and ref target the **table**, not that wrapper. Size the surrounding layout to constrain the scrolling region. `TableHead` and `TableCell` keep upstream's no-wrap and checkbox alignment styles. Rows retain hover, `data-state="selected"` and descendant `aria-expanded` feedback. ## Motion contract T0: no motion recipe, hook, provider, or animation runtime. All modes render the same static table. Row colour feedback is the upstream CSS colour transition; rows do not enter, reorder, resize, or animate selection. | Mode | Animated properties | | --- | --- | | full | none | | reduced | none | | none | none | No timing token or interruption lifecycle applies. ## Accessibility - Native table, row, header, cell and caption semantics remain intact. Provide a meaningful caption or an accessible name and use `scope` for header relationships. - Static rows and cells stay out of the tab order. Links, buttons and checkboxes inside cells keep their native keyboard interaction; no grid arrow-key model is added. - The wrapper scrolls horizontally on narrow screens; columns are not removed. If keyboard scrolling needs an explicit focus stop across your target browsers, pass `tabIndex={0}` to the named table with a visible focus ring, as in Usage. This supplies a focusable descendant of the scrolling container; arrow keys can scroll that ancestor without adding grid keyboard semantics. - No layout measurement or data processing runs. Render large datasets through application-owned pagination or virtualization; the server markup remains native HTML. ## Responsiveness and performance The table fills its container, which provides native horizontal scrolling when columns need more width. The caller owns column sizing, wrapping and any sticky behavior. Rows are all rendered; large datasets need application pagination or virtualization. T0 adds no authored animation runtime or interpolation. This wrapper renders HTML/CSS; interactive children and application handlers still need their own client code. Server-rendered markup does not imply that every interaction works without JavaScript. The registry enforces a 4 KiB gzip budget for this item's own shipped source; dependencies and application bundles are measured separately. ## Notes for AI - Preserve the table hierarchy: caption, header, body and footer belong inside Table. - Class names and refs on Table address the table; constrain its parent for overflow. - Table does not fetch data, validate values, sort, filter, paginate or own selection. - Do not add decorative row entrance or reorder motion to this T0 component.
